title: WPMS/2658/2016 of NATTHU LAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
ON THE 7TH DAY OF APRIL, 2021
BEFORE:
HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2658 of 2016
BETWEEN:
Natthu Lal ...Petitioner
(By Mr. M.K. Ray, Advocate)
AND:
State of Uttarakhand & others ...Respondents
(By Mr. T.S. Phartiyal, learned Additional C.S.C. for the
State of Uttarakhand.
JUDGMENT
Petitioner is challenging the order passed
by Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Udham Singh Nagar on
25.07.2015 whereby "Permanent Resident Certificate"
issued to the petitioner has been cancelled.
2. The ground taken for cancelling
"Permanent Resident Certificate" of the petitioner was
that he obtained the certificate by producing forged
documents. It has further been held that petitioner
could not produce any evidence to show that he was
residing at the given address fifteen years before
grant of "Permanent Resident Certificate".
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that petitioner was residing with one Mr. Jamna
Prasad S/o Lalta Prasad in Indra Colony, Rudrapur
since 1987 and petitioner's name was also mentioned

2
in the Ration Card issued in favour of Sri Jamna
Prasad.
4. This Court does not find any reason to
interfere with the cancellation order of Permanent
Resident Certificate of the petitioner. Merely, because
petitioner's name was included in the Ration Card,
issued in favour of one of his relatives residing in
Rudrapur, cannot be sufficient to declare him a
permanent resident of Rudrpur. For grant of
"Permanent Resident Certificate" certain conditions
have been prescribed in the Government Order.
Since petitioner did not fulfil those conditions,
therefore, Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Rudrapur was
justified in cancelling the "Permanent Resident
Certificate" issued in favour of the petitioner.
5. In such view of the matter, writ petition
fails and is hereby dismissed. However, petitioner
shall be at liberty to apply before the Competent
Authority for grant of "Permanent Resident
Certificate" as and when he completes the
requirements in terms of the Government Order.
 (MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI, J.)
Aswal
